newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BRUSSELS BOURSE RUNS OUT OF PUFF, INVESTORS PONDER.
newsitem.headline: BRUSSELS BOURSE RUNS OUT OF PUFF, INVESTORS PONDER.

text.p: The Brussels bourse ran out of steam on Friday and headed into the red in generally quiet dealings, with investors undecided whether to cash in their profits, take new long positions or simply to wait and see.
"The market is hesitant. People are reassessing their positions. They don't know whether to go long again or simply to wait for new figures to give a clue to the next step," one trader said.
"I get the impression that Belgium is having more difficulties than other markets in Europe. It has no energy to move up again," he added.

Traders said the combination of some pressure on long term interest rates, the overnight decline in the Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI and the slightly weaker dollar had compounded the general nervy air.
That, and the forecast of good weather in Belgium for the weekend, was keeping players out of the market, they added.
The Bel-20 index of blue chip shares was 22.73 points or 0.92 percent off at 2,457.04 at 0920 GMT with just 700 million francs worth of Belgian shares traded.
Cement maker CBR was the leading loser, down 3.6 percent, but traders reported some emerging buying interest.
Steel cord and wire firm Bekaert was close behind, down 3.30 percent on what traders said was a profit-taking driven correction.
Retailer Colruyt was down 1.9 percent, and insurer Fortis AG was down 2.0 percent after a price squeeze on Thursday.
Steelmaker Cockerill Sambre, a strong performer earlier in the week, was off 1.8 percent, and fellow steelmaker Arbed was down 0.9 percent.
Construction firm Franki, however, bucked the trend, climbing 3.75 percent.
